article.text:
## 2.1.323
- Added Code Mode, an experimental opt-in in which Claude writes JavaScript to call its tools; see https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-mode to turn it on, or to turn it off for an organization
- Added `engines["claude-code"]` to `plugin.json`: plugins outside their stated Claude Code version range are not installed, updated or loaded, and install and update pick the newest version that fits
- Added type checking of a plugin's TypeScript hooks module to `claude plugin validate`; each finding is a warning, and `--strict` fails on it
- Added to `claude plugin validate` the `$` nouns a mod's `engine.create` hook adds, withholds or replaces
- Added support for `CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_MODEL` in managed settings for Claude Desktop sessions on third-party providers (takes effect once Claude Desktop includes this version)
- Added an options menu (stop, switch to usage credits, upgrade) when a model needs usage credits that are turned off or used up
- Added a progress heartbeat every 30 seconds while hooks run long in `claude -p` and SDK sessions, so a host such as Claude Desktop won't end the turn as hung (once it includes this version)
- Added `.docx` support to Artifact tool asset uploads
- Added a `/diff to close` hint to the diff panel, and the keys that focus and close a panel to the `?` shortcut guide
- Added a start-up warning for Bash allow rules with a `*` in a variable's value, such as `Bash(PORT=* npm run dev)`
- Added a warning when a plugin's language server can't start, naming the server and what to check
- Added a one-time startup notice naming `CLAUDE_CODE_PERFORCE_MODE` when Perforce settings are found and the mode is off
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AGENT_PROGRESS_SUMMARIES` (available since 2.1.318): set it to `1` to turn off subagent progress summaries and the requests that write them (anthropics/claude-code#86879)
- Added `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_HINT_COMMAND`, which a program that starts Claude Code can set to have the exit hint name its own resume command
- Added `unsetOptionCount` to the `claude plugin install --json` result: how many `userConfig` options are not yet set
- Added `isPromptCovered` to the props a mod's pane is drawn with, telling it when a dialog or a field above the prompt covers the prompt
- Fixed running `/compact` again, or after a command such as `/context`, summarizing away a message that Claude had not answered yet
- Fixed a resumed session joining your next message to an old interrupted message that was not resumed
- Fixed a memory spike at the next prompt after Claude changed a very large file
- Fixed a setting saved in a running session undoing a hand edit made to `settings.json` moments earlier; a settings file you delete during a session now stays deleted
- Fixed `claude plugin` commands and `claude mcp list` signing you out of a Console profile when they ended while the token was being renewed
- Fixed Edit and Bash running out of memory on certain `/proc` files, and Edit hanging or running out of memory on devices and named pipes
- Fixed Claude Code failing to start, or to clear stored credentials at sign-out, when saving its configuration file failed with "Out of memory"
- Fixed requests sent without streaming failing on errors that streamed requests recover from, such as a rejected image, thinking block or beta header
- Fixed `ExitWorktree`, the worktree exit dialog and `/resume` leaving the session in the wrong folder when the folder the shell was in before entering the worktree had been deleted
- Fixed accents and other combining marks sometimes landing left of the text, leaving stale copies on screen, or silently disappearing when text wraps
- Fixed the last key of a key chord, such as Enter in ctrl+x enter, acting on a dialog's text field when the chord's own action isn't available there
- Fixed `ps` processes piling up when the process listing Claude Code runs before stopping a command takes too long
- Fixed subagent transcripts and large tool results being saved apart…

Nov 13, 2026v2.3.0
Background Subagents by Default
Subagents now return immediately, continue in the background, and report back whenever they become idle. You can keep working in the parent session while multiple subagents run concurrently.#63382
Quieter Transcripts by Default
The TUI now summarizes each run of tool calls and thoughts into one collapsible activity row, so the answer is easier to follow. To see every step again, set Verbosity to medium or high in settings, or set session.verbosity in your TUI config; an existing setting is kept.#63207
Jump to an Earlier Prompt
In the desktop app, open Jump to message from the command palette or press Cmd+Alt+G (Ctrl+Alt+G on Windows and Linux) to search prompts across the current session and jump directly to one.#63585
Improvements 32
32 more improvements
Fixes 34
34 more fixes
Nov 10, 2026v2.2.7
GitHub Copilot Auto
Pick Auto in the model picker when your Copilot account has an Auto pool, and Copilot's router chooses the model for each session at the Auto discount. If routing fails, OpenCode falls back to the account's default chat model.#62997
Side Panel Tab Shortcuts
Right-click a side panel tab and choose Close tabs to the right. ⌘W now closes side panel tabs wherever focus is, ⌥⌘W or Ctrl+Alt+W always closes the session tab, and ⌘⇧T reopens the last closed tab of either kind where it was.#62922
Mark Sessions Read or Unread
Open the menu on a tab, Home row, project row or inbox card and choose Mark as unread to keep its dot until you next visit.#62889
Breaking changes
@opencode/ai: ImageResponse.image is removed
This affects code that imports @opencode/ai directly. Read response.images[0] instead of response.image.
#63011
SDK: fewer endpoints wait for plugins to load
On a Location that is still loading plugins, agent.list returns the agents loaded so far, and integration.list, usage.limits, vcs.init, rpc.call and artifact.* no longer wait up to 5 seconds. Entries and actions that a plugin provides appear when it finishes loading, so refresh on the matching *.updated event. Model, provider, generate.*, voice.* and websearch.query endpoints still wait.

Shared MCP Connections
Turn on pooling for an MCP server to share one connection across projects with the same setup, so you run fewer processes and start faster.#61185
GUI Plugin Themes and New Slots
GUI plugins can now add color themes, render or add actions to code blocks, and use native settings and menu components.#61485#61533#61527#61509
Mobile Composer Dock
On phones and tablets, composer actions now sit in a touch dock above the keyboard with larger buttons.#61773
Scripted Runs in Worktrees
Run opencode run -w to start the session in a new git worktree, or --worktree=<name> to name it.#60712

Add --archived to opencode run to keep scripted and CI sessions out of your inbox and session lists.#61270

Press ⌘⌥O on macOS or Ctrl+Alt+O on Windows and Linux to choose a worktree, and ⌘⌥B or Ctrl+Alt+B to choose its base branch. ⌘⇧X or Ctrl+Shift+X now toggles shell mode in the composer.#60713

article.title: The Brave Search API now accepts agentic payments via the x402 protocol | Brave
article.text:
The Brave Search API now accepts agentic payments via the x402 protocol
Published
Nov 12, 2026
Share on X (formerly Twitter)
Share on Reddit
Share on Telegram
Share on LinkedIn
Brave Search news
The Brave Search API, our developer tool for building applications with data from the Web, is adding support for instant, pay-as-you-go, agentic payments enabled by the open x402 payment protocol. Developers and autonomous AI agents that specifically require agentic search can now programmatically query Brave’s independent search index, ground agent responses, and settle requests in real time, which eliminates the need for traditional API key management.
Integrating x402 with the Brave Search API makes it easier for an agentic harness to leverage Brave Search API via a CLI wallet, as Brave runs its own facilitator accepting USDC on the Base blockchain, with acceptance on other networks and with other stablecoins incoming soon. This allows a Brave Search API user the ability to pay for LLM Context (agentic grounding) or general web search on-demand, without first creating an account and selecting a plan. Instead, simply transfer USDC stablecoin to your agent’s wallet via the Base network and it’s ready to access the same high-quality search results powered by Brave’s search engine.
How does it work?
Brave Search API endpoints behind x402 require payment on every request rather than authentication. A request sent without payment receives an HTTP 402 Payment Required response that states the price of that search and the payment details needed to pay it. The agent signs a USDC payment for that amount and retries the request with the signed payment attached. Once the payment is verified, the search runs and results are returned with a receipt of the transaction that occurred on the Base blockchain.
Get started today
Pricing follows Brave’s published API rates: LLM Context, an API designed specifically for providing search context for agents, will cost $0.005 ($5 per 1,000). Additionally, web (search for humans), news, image, video, and local endpoints will also be available for $0.005 ($5 per 1,000). Gas fees for transacting on the Base blockchain will be covered for a limited time. Since each request carries its own payment, a Brave Search API account is no longer needed to use the service.
The easiest path to query via x402 is to install Purl Wallet, a Stripe-developed CLI wallet for your agent. Set up your wallet, top it off using Base-native USDC, and start querying today.
Ready to build pay-as-you-go search into your apps or AI agents? Check out our Brave Search x402 Proxy Documentation and explore: https://api-dashboard.search.brave.com/documentation/guides/agent-payments

GitHub Enterprise Server support in the GitHub Copilot app
You can now bring your work on GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) into the GitHub Copilot app. Add your GHES account to work with remote repositories, issues, and pull requests. This feature was previously an opt-in preview, and is now generally available.
You’ll need to sign in with a GitHub.com or GHE.com account first. Then, go to Settings > Accounts > Add account and choose GitHub Enterprise Server.
Available in GitHub Copilot app 1.2.0 and later. Cloud sessions aren’t available for GHES. Learn more in our Copilot GHES documentation.
